# Synthesis

## A. The 3–4 dominant idioms in 2026

**1. The hero *is* the install command, and the version number lives in the button.**
Bun (`Install Bun v1.3.14` + Linux/macOS↔Windows toggle), Atuin (copy-box + `$ get-started`), Astro (`npm create astro@latest`, "Copied!"), Tauri (9-way package-manager tabs), Starship (install block inlined on the homepage). Nobody makes you click through to a getting-started page to see the command. Corollary: **Ghostty's download page, which offers no copy-command, is the outlier and it reads as friction.**

**2. Product surfaces are re-rendered in the DOM, not screenshotted.**
Zed's activity feed + code pane with real inline diagnostics; Atuin's `demo-term`; Biome's rendered diagnostic block; Warp's interactive configurator; Bun's syntax-highlighted API carousel. Benefits: crisp at every DPI, selectable/copyable, themeable, dark/light-reactive, diffable in git, and localizable. **PNG screenshots now read as dated** — which is precisely what Starship's presets page and Oh My Posh's theme gallery both are.

**3. Dark-first, but with *zoned* dark rather than one flat black.**
Ghostty `#0f0f11` dark-only; ray.so `#0d0d0d`; Warp stacks `#0b0b0b`/`#111111`/`#1f1f1f` and then adds **tinted section washes** (`#1e142a` purple, `#141e30` blue, `#1a2a1a` green, `#201a14` amber) to color-code content zones; Atuin `#0f1722` with a green/warm-cream dual accent. The 2026 refinement over 2023 is calibrated multi-step neutral ramps plus one saturated accent — **not** gradient-mesh, not glassmorphism, not noise/grain (I found essentially none of those in this cohort). Motion is minimal and confined to hero and section transitions.

**4. Typography is now the brand.**
Zed runs four self-hosted families (IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Serif, iA Writer Quattro S, Lilex). Ghostty picked Pretendard Variable. Atuin picked DM Sans + Space Mono. Bun deliberately uses `system-ui`. The tools that read as "default template" are exactly the ones on stock Inter over a stock generator theme — **Starship and Oh My Posh both sit in that bucket.** For a prompt engine specifically: **Starship prepends `"Nerd Font"` to its mono stack** so glyphs render in code blocks; that is a one-line, high-leverage steal.

**Emerging fifth idiom — the agent affordance.** Bun (`/docs/llms.txt`), Zed (`/docs/llms.txt` **plus a `.md` version of every page**, advertised in-page). This is becoming table stakes and is cheap on any generator.

## B. Navigating a large reference surface — what actually works

Observed strategies, ranked by how well they hold up:

| Strategy | Who | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **Split the reference by axis before listing** (language × category) | Biome: 5 language pages × 9 groups | **Best.** No single page exceeds ~80 rows. |
| **Facet dropdown over a card grid** | Tauri plugins (platform filter + `Ctrl+K`) | **Best-in-cohort interaction.** Only site that filters in the browser. |
| **Group by provenance/domain, table per group** | Ruff (~50 linter groups), Biome | Scales to ~900 rows but is scroll-and-find, not filter. |
| **Generated reference as its own searchable app** | Bun `/reference` (from TS types, own search field) | **Strong** — separates hand-written prose from machine truth, and never drifts. |
| **Second re-cut of the same catalog** | Biome "Recommended rules" by severity; Ruff "Default rules" | Cheap, high value — serves a different intent from the same data. |
| **Capability matrix table** | Tauri plugin × 5 platforms | Excellent for cross-cutting support questions. |
| Single giant page + right-hand TOC | Starship `/config/` (~100 modules) | **Breaks.** TOC is unusable at this length. |
| Single giant page + "use browser find" | Ghostty config reference | **Breaks, and maintainers say so in the page.** |
| Static table, discovery offloaded to CLI/TUI | mise registry (1000+ tools) | Defensible for a CLI, **fails as a web discovery surface.** |

**The pattern that keeps recurring in the ones that work**: metadata rendered as a **badge column** rather than prose — Biome (✓ recommended / 🔧 safe fix / ⚠️ unsafe fix / 🔮 next release, with a legend), Ruff (stable/preview/deprecated/removed + 🛠️ auto-fix), Ghostty (**"Available since: 1.2.0"** and platform-scope notes per option). Badges are scannable, filterable if you later add JS, and answer "can I use this yet?" without opening the page.

**Ordering**: Ghostty orders options **by frequency of use and semantic grouping, not alphabetically**. Oh My Posh's segment sidebar is alphabetical-within-category; frequency ordering (or a "most used" cluster) would surface `git`, `path`, `python`, `node` above `argocd`.

## C. Theme gallery / showcase patterns

**The reference implementation is ray.so/themes** (Raycast's Theme Explorer, open source at `raycast/ray-so`). Verified in-browser:
- **Live-rendered preview, not a screenshot** — the actual app chrome ("Search for apps and commands…", list rows, primary text) rendered in the theme's own colors, in DOM.
- **Dark / Light segmented toggle** at gallery level, each linking to a representative theme (`/chris/almost-cyan`, `/luxonauta/alucard`).
- **URL is `/{author}/{theme-slug}`** — every theme is individually addressable and shareable; theme state is encoded in the URL.
- **One-click "Add to Raycast"** deep-link — zero copy-paste between browse and apply. This is the single biggest conversion lever and nothing in the Oh My Posh cohort has it.
- Authoring loop closed: Theme Studio → right-click → *Copy as URL* (produces a gallery link) or *Copy as JSON*. **The gallery is the sharing format.**
- Dark `#0d0d0d`, Inter, Radix-style grey scales (`gray-2`…`gray-12`, `gray-a4`…`gray-a11`), pill/`rounded-md` radii.

Supporting patterns:
- **Card anatomy** (Astro themes, Vercel templates): thumbnail · title · 1–2 line description · **author avatar + name** · status pill. Authorship is what makes a community gallery feel like a community.
- **Faceted sidebar with per-facet counts and a global "Clear"**, URL-driven so filter state is shareable/bookmarkable — Vercel `/templates` is the model (Use Case / Framework / CSS / Database / Auth / CMS, each with a selected-count indicator).
- **Tiering**: Tauri's official-cards-vs-community-links, Astro's featured/sponsor row. Useful, but see anti-patterns.
- **Screenshot cards linking to per-item pages** — Starship presets. Minimum viable; what Oh My Posh has today, minus even the per-item page.

**Concrete implication for an Oh My Posh theme gallery**: render prompts as HTML/CSS from the theme JSON (segments, colors, powerline separators, Nerd Font glyphs) instead of committing 150 PNGs; give each theme `/themes/{name}`; facet by *needs Nerd Font · has powerline · segment count · light/dark · segments used*; add a one-click apply (copy `oh-my-posh init pwsh --config <url>` or a deep link); and let the same renderer power previews on segment reference pages.

## D. Anti-patterns to avoid

1. **Logo-only hero for a visual product.** Starship and Biome both lead with a logo. If the product's value is what appears on screen, the hero must show it. Atuin, Zed, and Bun all do.
2. **Screenshot galleries.** 150 PNGs are stale on merge, unfilterable, un-themeable, invisible to search, and heavy. Render from source data.
3. **The monolithic reference page.** Starship's `/config/` and Ghostty's config reference are the two clearest failures in this study — and Ghostty's own docs concede it.
4. **Catalogs with no in-browser filter.** Ruff (900 rules), Biome (511), mise (1000 tools), Astro themes (hundreds) — all rely on browser find or an external search. Tauri's platform dropdown is the lone counterexample and it's trivially cheap.
5. **A JS-only homepage.** ghostty.org served me an empty `<main>` with a browser attached. Whatever agents, crawlers, and link previews see, that's what they see too. Anything above the fold should be in the HTML.
6. **Enterprise mega-menu drift.** Warp's `Solutions › Industry › Insurance` taxonomy on what people still install as a terminal. For an OSS tool, a 4–6 item nav (Atuin: History · AI · Blog · Docs; Ghostty: Docs · Discord · GitHub · Download) is correct.
7. **Sponsored-first gallery ordering.** Astro's themes page is 12+ "Paid" cards deep before community work appears. Corrosive to an OSS community gallery.
8. **Version-number headlines.** "Tauri 2.0" tells a first-time visitor nothing. Put the version in the install button (Bun) instead.
9. **Un-themed default generators.** Stock VitePress with one swapped brand color (Starship), stock Material for MkDocs (uv, ruff), stock Docusaurus (Oh My Posh). Instantly legible as "we didn't design this." The cheapest fix with the largest return is **type + a calibrated neutral ramp**, not illustration.
10. **Emoji as sidebar taxonomy.** Oh My Posh's `💡 Getting Started` / `✨ Prompt` doesn't survive translation, search indexing, or scanning at density.

The shell/posh logo suggests keeping blue but making it more specific to the brand, possibly paired with a warm accent for the powerline elements. Rose-pine-moon's base color is already in use for code, so I could lean into that palette with a rose or gold accent to create cohesion. I'm planning to build a comprehensive design proposal document with actual HTML mockups for each direction, current state audit, condensed competitor findings, information architecture trees, and a phased recommendation — it's a substantial piece of work, but the design quality is important enough to warrant doing it properly. Writing design tokens...

For the structure, I'm thinking headings in a tight sans with negative tracking, labels in monospace uppercase, and body copy in system sans—that monospace choice feels authentic to the subject rather than decorative. Instead of relying on a Nerd Font for powerline chevrons, I can use CSS clip-path to create angled chevron geometry directly, which keeps the design self-contained and subject-specific. The document itself will flow through a header with title and metadata, audit findings with numbers, a condensed competitor landscape plus the four key idioms, and then navigation architecture options.

For the visual centerpiece, I'm rendering three mini homepage mockups in the DOM—each around 500 pixels tall showing nav, hero, and install box—plus segment catalog and theme gallery mockups for the later directions. The key insight is that each mockup needs its own isolated visual world with its own palette, so they shouldn't inherit the page theme. I'll scope each one independently so the directions feel distinct and self-contained.

Now I'm mapping out the three directions: Direction A keeps the Docusaurus aesthetic with a calibrated blue palette and light-first approach; Direction B goes dark with terminal-inspired geometry and animated prompts; Direction C treats the whole site as an interactive config studio with a split-screen edit interface.

I'm building the HTML mockup with a fake terminal prompt rendered in DOM using CSS clip-path to create powerline chevron segments for user, host, path, git branch, node version, and timestamp with ANSI-style colors. I'll add a favicon emoji and metadata, keeping the markup thorough but concise.

Now I'm sketching out three information architecture options: a "Tidy" version that fixes the current structure, a "Four doors" approach reorganizing into Start/Configure/Reference/Community with themes and segments as top-level products, and a "Task-first" model navigating by user intent with Install, Customize, Reference, Gallery, and Community sections. Let me flesh these out with concrete details, starting with the Four doors structure that promotes themes and segments to the main navigation.

For the sidebar under that model, I'm organizing content into Start here covering installation across platforms and initial setup, Configure for all the customization options like blocks and segments, Reference for the comprehensive indexes and schemas, Integrate for connecting external tools, and Troubleshoot for common issues.

I'm also proposing that Themes and Segments become top-level site sections with their own galleries and catalogs rather than staying buried in the docs. Now I'm ready to write out the full artifact in a single pass without the HTML boilerplate.

<style>
/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Document shell tokens
   Neutral ramp carries a slight blue-slate bias, borrowed from

:root {

  --mono: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", "Cascadia Mono", "Cascadia Code", "JetBrains Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace;
  --sans: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif;

  --measure: 68ch;

}

@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {

    --ink-3:      #7b8798;

    --rule-soft:  #1d242e;
    --accent:     #63a4f0;
    --accent-ink: #a8caf7;
    --accent-wash:#15243a;
    --amber:      #e0ac5a;
    --amber-wash: #2a2115;

    --bad:        #e07a6e;
  }
}

:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  --ink:        #e3e9f2;
  --ink-2:      #a5b1c2;
  --ink-3:      #7b8798;
  --ground:     #0e1117;
  --panel:      #151a22;
  --rule:       #262e3a;
  --rule-soft:  #1d242e;
  --accent:     #63a4f0;
  --accent-ink: #a8caf7;
  --accent-wash:#15243a;

  --amber-wash: #2a2115;

}

:root[data-theme="light"] {
  --ink:        #131820;
  --ink-2:      #3d4757;
  --ink-3:      #6b7788;
  --ground:     #f7f8fa;
  --panel:      #ffffff;
  --rule:       #dde2ea;
  --rule-soft:  #e9edf3;

  --accent-ink: #0f4c96;
  --accent-wash:#e8f0fb;

  --amber-wash: #fdf3e0;
  --good:       #1a7f52;
  --bad:        #b4453a;
}

/* ── base ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.doc {
  background: var(--ground);
  color: var(--ink);
  font-family: var(--sans);
  font-size: 16px;
  line-height: 1.6;
  -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
}
.doc *,
.doc *::before,
.doc *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }

.wrap {

  margin: 0 auto;
  padding: 0 var(--pad);
}

.doc h1, .doc h2, .doc h3, .doc h4 {
  text-wrap: balance;
  letter-spacing: -0.018em;
  line-height: 1.15;
  margin: 0;
  font-weight: 640;
}

.doc p { margin: 0; max-width: var(--measure); }
.doc a { color: var(--accent); text-decoration-thickness: 1px; text-underline-offset: 2px; }
.doc a:focus-visible,

/* Eyebrow — monospace is the subject's own vernacular, used only

.eyebrow {

.stack   { display: flex; flex-direction: column; }

/* ── findings ───────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.stat-grid {
  display: grid;

.stat .n.warn { color: var(--bad); }

.findings { display: grid; gap: 1px; background: var(--rule); border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 8px; overflow: hidden; }
.finding {
  background: var(--panel);
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 7.5rem 1fr;
  gap: 0 1.25rem;
  padding: 0.95rem 1.15rem;

}
.finding .sev {
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-size: 0.66rem;
  letter-spacing: 0.1em;

.sev.block { background: var(--bad); color: #fff; }

.finding code { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.86em; background: var(--rule-soft); padding: 0.08em 0.32em; border-radius: 3px; }
@media (max-width: 620px) {
  .finding { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 0.45rem; }
}

/* ── tables ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.tbl-scroll { overflow-x: auto; border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--panel); }
table.t { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 0.88rem; min-width: 640px; }

.verdict { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.74rem; white-space: nowrap; }
.verdict.up { color: var(--good); }
.verdict.down { color: var(--bad); }

/* ── IA trees ───────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.ia-grid { display: grid; gap: 1.25rem; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(310px, 1fr)); align-items: start; }

      <h2 style="font-size:1.65rem;">The homepage is still the 2020 Docusaurus scaffold</h2>
      <p class="lede">
        Two buttons, three emoji paragraphs, one static PNG — about 130 lines total. Everything that would
        make a visitor install has to be found somewhere else.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="stat-grid">
      <div class="stat"><span class="n">130</span><span class="l">lines in the entire homepage</span></div>
      <div class="stat"><span class="n">11</span><span class="l">top-level sidebar entries, all emoji-prefixed</span></div>
      <div class="stat"><span class="n warn">28,093<span style="font-size:0.6em">px</span></span><span class="l">height of the themes page — 124 PNGs, 8 MB, no filter</span></div>
      <div class="stat"><span class="n warn">0</span><span class="l">segment reference pages showing what the segment looks like</span></div>

    </div>

    <div class="stack gap-4">
      <h3 style="font-size:1.05rem;">Concrete defects found in the codebase</h3>
      <div class="findings">
        <div class="finding">
          <span class="sev block">Blocking</span>
          <p><b>“Get Started →” lands on a theory page.</b> <code>configuration/introduction.mdx</code> carries <code>slug: /</code>, so the primary homepage CTA opens an essay about blocks and segments — not an install command. The sidebar’s actual first item is Getting Started › Installation › Windows, which the CTA never reaches.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="finding">
          <span class="sev block">Blocking</span>
          <p><b>No index pages exist.</b> Getting Started, Segments, and all eight segment sub-groups are bare categories — clicking them only expands a tree. <code>static/llms.txt</code> already links <code>/docs/segments/overview</code> and <code>/docs/configuration/overview</code>; neither page exists, and <code>onBrokenLinks: 'ignore'</code> hides it.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="finding">
          <span class="sev block">Blocking</span>
          <p><b>Segment discovery depends on guessing a bucket.</b> <code>kubectl</code>, <code>helm</code> and <code>argocd</code> live under CLI, not Cloud. <code>docker</code> is CLI. <code>winget</code> is System. Every group is <code>collapsed: true</code> by default, so the default view of 117 segments shows nothing.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="finding">
          <span class="sev friction">Friction</span>
          <p><b>The theme gallery is one 124-image scroll.</b> No search, no tags, no filter, no per-theme URL, no way to apply one. The Nerd-Font requirement is a sentence of prose, not a facet. It is also one of only two homepage CTAs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="finding">
          <span class="sev friction">Friction</span>
          <p><b>The FAQ absorbs everything with no home.</b> 24 headings covering PowerShell, fonts, Windows Terminal, JetBrains, Conda, venv, Zsh, Fish, Xonsh, Vim and posh-git. There is no troubleshooting section, no per-shell page and no per-terminal page.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="finding">
          <span class="sev friction">Friction</span>
          <p><b>Orphan and near-orphan docs.</b> <code>docs/auth.mdx</code> is in no sidebar — only reachable via an OAuth redirect. <code>Advanced</code> is a category with exactly one child. <code>dsc</code>, <code>themes</code>, <code>share</code>, <code>faq</code>, <code>migrating</code> and <code>contributors</code> float loose at root.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="finding">
          <span class="sev friction">Friction</span>
          <p><b>Navbar priorities are inverted.</b> Sponsor and Swag sit in primary left nav beside Docs and Blog, above a non-closeable sponsor bar. The blog has averaged under one post a year since 2022. Themes and Segments — the two things people actually come for — are not in the nav at all.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="finding">
          <span class="sev polish">Polish</span>
          <p><b>The CSS has hash-coupled selectors.</b> <code>a.getStarted_Sjon</code> and <code>.themedImage_ToTc</code> target generated CSS-module hashes and break silently on upgrade. <code>--ifm-color-primary-lightest</code> is <code>rgb(8,9,10)</code> — near-black. <code>--ifm-font-family-monospace</code> is set to <code>"Inter"</code>. Fira Code is fetched from Google Fonts and never referenced.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

        <thead>

        </thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Effort</td><td>Days</td><td>Weeks</td><td>A quarter, incremental</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Platform</td><td>Docusaurus, unchanged</td><td>Docusaurus + custom React pages</td><td>Docusaurus for prose, app for the rest</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Pairs with</td><td>IA-1</td><td>IA-2</td><td>IA-3</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Kills the PNG gallery</td><td class="verdict down">no</td><td class="verdict up">yes — DOM renders</td><td class="verdict up">yes — editable renders</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Segment previews</td><td class="verdict down">no</td><td class="verdict up">static live render</td><td class="verdict up">interactive</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Visually distinct from Starship</td><td>somewhat</td><td class="verdict up">decisively</td><td class="verdict up">no comparison</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Maintenance load</td><td>lower than today</td><td>renderer to maintain</td><td>a real app to maintain</td></tr>

        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>

      piece in both — build it once, behind a stable interface that takes a config object and mock context and returns

            <li>Delete the hash-coupled CSS selectors; fix <code>--ifm-font-family-monospace</code>; drop the unused Fira Code request; correct <code>--ifm-color-primary-lightest</code>.</li>
            <li>Prepend <code>"Nerd Font"</code> to the monospace stack.</li>
            <li>Put <code>auth.mdx</code> in the sidebar; collapse the one-child Advanced category.</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="phase">
        <span class="no">Phase 1</span>
        <div>
          <h4>Homepage and nav</h4>
          <p>Direction B applied to the two highest-traffic surfaces.</p>
          <ul>
            <li>Rebuild the hero: install box with OS toggle, version in the button, DOM-rendered prompt.</li>
            <li>Promote Themes and Segments into primary nav; move Sponsor, Swag and Blog into Community.</li>
            <li>Retire the non-closeable announcement bar in favour of a footer sponsor block.</li>
            <li>Token pass: neutral ramp, type scale, chevron geometry, zoned dark sections.</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="phase">
        <span class="no">Phase 2</span>
        <div>
          <h4>The renderer</h4>
          <p>The load-bearing investment. One function: config + mock context → DOM.</p>
          <ul>
            <li>Reuse <code>segment_data.json</code> as the fixture context; it already covers every segment.</li>
            <li>Verify fidelity against the Go engine in CI — render every bundled theme both ways and diff the ANSI.</li>
            <li>Ship it first as a build-time renderer, so there is no client-side cost yet.</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="phase">
        <span class="no">Phase 3</span>
        <div>
          <h4>Catalogs</h4>
          <p>Point the renderer at the two large surfaces.</p>
          <ul>
            <li><code>/themes</code>: faceted gallery, per-theme URLs, live renders, one-click apply command. Deletes 8 MB of PNGs.</li>
            <li><code>/segments</code>: faceted catalog with badge column, each card previewing its own output.</li>
            <li>Embed the same preview at the top of every segment reference page.</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="phase">
        <span class="no">Phase 4</span>
        <div>
          <h4>Docs restructure</h4>
          <p>IA-2 in full, once the two catalogs have left <code>/docs</code>.</p>
          <ul>
            <li>Split the FAQ into Troubleshooting by shell, terminal and editor.</li>
            <li>Separate hand-written Configure prose from a generated Reference tier — the Bun split.</li>
            <li>Drop emoji from sidebar labels; order segments by usage, not alphabet.</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="phase">
        <span class="no">Phase 5</span>
        <div>
          <h4>Studio, if the renderer holds up</h4>
          <p>Only worth starting once phases 2–3 have proven fidelity in production.</p>
          <ul>
            <li>Editor around the existing renderer; config encoded in the URL.</li>
            <li>“Open in Studio” from every theme and every segment page.</li>
            <li>Short-link service so <code>--config</code> can point at a shared prompt.</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ══════════════════════════════ OPEN ══════════════════════════════ -->
<section class="band">
  <div class="wrap stack gap-6">
    <div class="stack gap-3">
      <p class="eyebrow">07 — Open questions</p>
      <h2 style="font-size:1.65rem;">Decisions that change the plan</h2>
    </div>
    <div class="findings">
      <div class="finding"><span class="sev polish">Q1</span><p><b>Stay on Docusaurus?</b> Astro + Starlight is what Biome and Tauri run, and it makes custom app-like pages far cheaper than Docusaurus swizzling. Migrating 153 docs is real work but mostly mechanical. Direction B is doable either way; direction C is materially easier on Astro.</p></div>
      <div class="finding"><span class="sev polish">Q2</span><p><b>Second renderer, or compile the real one?</b> A JS renderer risks drifting from the Go engine. The alternative is compiling the engine to WASM and rendering the truth — heavier, but there is then only one implementation to trust.</p></div>
      <div class="finding"><span class="sev polish">Q3</span><p><b>Nerd Font glyphs on the web.</b> Live previews need a subset Nerd Font served from the site, or the powerline separators will render as tofu for most visitors. Licensing and weight both need a look.</p></div>
      <div class="finding"><span class="sev polish">Q4</span><p><b>Does the blog stay?</b> Six posts since 2022. Either fold it into a Community section alongside release notes, or retire it and let the changelog carry that job.</p></div>
      <div class="finding"><span class="sev polish">Q5</span><p><b>Where does sponsorship live?</b> The permanent announcement bar and the two primary-nav slots are the most valuable real estate on the site and currently earn less than a well-placed footer block would.</p></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<footer class="end">
  <div class="wrap">Analysis phase only — no code changed. Mockups are DOM, not images; view source to lift the chevron geometry.</div>
</footer>

</div>

:root[data-theme="light"] {
  --ink:        #131820;
  --ink-2:      #3d4757;
  --ink-3:      #6b7788;
  --ground:     #f7f8fa;
  --panel:      #ffffff;
  --rule:       #dde2ea;
  --rule-soft:  #e9edf3;
  --accent:     #1f6fd0;
  --accent-ink: #0f4c96;
  --accent-wash:#e8f0fb;
  --amber:      #a86b12;
  --amber-wash: #fdf3e0;
  --good:       #1a7f52;
  --bad:        #b4453a;
}

/* ── base ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.doc {
  background: var(--ground);
  color: var(--ink);
  font-family: var(--sans);
  font-size: 16px;
  line-height: 1.6;
  -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
}
.doc *,
.doc *::before,
.doc *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }

.wrap {
  max-width: 1120px;
  margin: 0 auto;
  padding: 0 var(--pad);
}

.doc h1, .doc h2, .doc h3, .doc h4 {
  text-wrap: balance;
  letter-spacing: -0.018em;
  line-height: 1.15;
  margin: 0;
  font-weight: 640;
}

.doc p { margin: 0; max-width: var(--measure); }
.doc a { color: var(--accent); text-decoration-thickness: 1px; text-underline-offset: 2px; }
.doc a:focus-visible,
.doc button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 3px; }

/* Eyebrow — monospace is the subject's own vernacular, used only
   as a structural marker, never as body text. */
.eyebrow {
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-size: 0.68rem;
  letter-spacing: 0.16em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--ink-3);
  margin: 0;
}

.stack   { display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
.gap-2   { gap: 0.5rem; }
.gap-3   { gap: 0.75rem; }
.gap-4   { gap: 1rem; }
.gap-6   { gap: 1.5rem; }
.gap-8   { gap: 2rem; }

section.band { padding: clamp(2.75rem, 6vw, 4.5rem) 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule-soft); }
section.band:first-of-type { border-top: 0; }

.lede { font-size: 1.075rem; color: var(--ink-2); }
.small { font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--ink-2); }
.tiny { font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--ink-3); }

/* ── masthead ───────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.masthead {
  padding: clamp(3rem, 8vw, 5.5rem) 0 clamp(2rem, 4vw, 3rem);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule);
}
.masthead h1 {
  font-size: clamp(2rem, 5.2vw, 3.1rem);
  max-width: 20ch;
}
.masthead .lede { max-width: 60ch; font-size: 1.15rem; }

.meta-row {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 0.5rem 1.75rem;
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-size: 0.75rem;
  color: var(--ink-3);
  border-top: 1px solid var(--rule-soft);
  padding-top: 1rem;
}
.meta-row b { color: var(--ink-2); font-weight: 500; }

/* ── findings ───────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.stat-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(160px, 1fr));
  gap: 1px;
  background: var(--rule);
  border: 1px solid var(--rule);
  border-radius: 8px;
  overflow: hidden;
}
.stat {
  background: var(--panel);
  padding: 1.1rem 1.15rem;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 0.3rem;
}
.stat .n {
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-size: 1.6rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  letter-spacing: -0.03em;
  color: var(--ink);
}
.stat .n.warn { color: var(--bad); }
.stat .l { font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--ink-3); line-height: 1.35; }

.findings { display: grid; gap: 1px; background: var(--rule); border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 8px; overflow: hidden; }
.finding {
  background: var(--panel);
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 7.5rem 1fr;
  gap: 0 1.25rem;
  padding: 0.95rem 1.15rem;
  align-items: baseline;
}
.finding .sev {
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-size: 0.66rem;
  letter-spacing: 0.1em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  padding: 0.15rem 0.45rem;
  border-radius: 3px;
  justify-self: start;
  white-space: nowrap;
}
.sev.block { background: var(--bad); color: #fff; }
.sev.friction { background: var(--amber-wash); color: var(--amber); border: 1px solid currentColor; }
.sev.polish { background: var(--rule-soft); color: var(--ink-3); }
.finding p { font-size: 0.92rem; }
.finding code { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.86em; background: var(--rule-soft); padding: 0.08em 0.32em; border-radius: 3px; }
@media (max-width: 620px) {
  .finding { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 0.45rem; }
}

/* ── tables ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.tbl-scroll { overflow-x: auto; border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--panel); }
table.t { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 0.88rem; min-width: 640px; }
table.t th, table.t td { text-align: left; padding: 0.7rem 0.9rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule-soft); vertical-align: top; }
table.t thead th {
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-size: 0.68rem;
  letter-spacing: 0.11em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--ink-3);
  font-weight: 500;
  background: var(--rule-soft);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule);
}
table.t tbody tr:last-child td { border-bottom: 0; }
table.t td:first-child { font-weight: 560; color: var(--ink); white-space: nowrap; }
.verdict { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.74rem; white-space: nowrap; }
.verdict.up { color: var(--good); }
.verdict.down { color: var(--bad); }

/* ── IA trees ───────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.ia-grid { display: grid; gap: 1.25rem; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(310px, 1fr)); align-items: start; }
.ia {
  background: var(--panel);
  border: 1px solid var(--rule);
  border-radius: 10px;
  overflow: hidden;
}
.ia > header { padding: 1rem 1.15rem 0.85rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule-soft); display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.35rem; }
.ia > header h3 { font-size: 1.02rem; }
.ia .tree {
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-size: 0.78rem;
  line-height: 1.75;
  padding: 0.9rem 1.15rem 1.15rem;
  margin: 0;
  white-space: pre;
  overflow-x: auto;
  color: var(--ink-2);
}
.ia .tree b { color: var(--ink); font-weight: 600; }
.ia .tree i { color: var(--good); font-style: normal; }
.ia .tree s { color: var(--ink-3); }
.ia footer { padding: 0.85rem 1.15rem 1.05rem; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule-soft); font-size: 0.85rem; color: var(--ink-2); }

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   MOCKUPS
   Each mockup is its own visual world with its own tokens.
   They deliberately ignore the document theme — they are
   artwork samples, not page chrome.
   ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.mock-frame {
  border: 1px solid var(--rule);
  border-radius: 12px;
  overflow: hidden;
  box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(10, 16, 26, 0.06), 0 12px 32px -20px rgba(10, 16, 26, 0.35);
}
.mock-caption {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 0.4rem 1rem;
  align-items: baseline;
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-size: 0.7rem;
  letter-spacing: 0.08em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--ink-3);
  padding: 0.6rem 0.15rem 0;
}

.mock { font-size: 15px; line-height: 1.5; }
.mock * { box-sizing: border-box; }
.mock .m-wrap { max-width: 980px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 0 1.75rem; }
.mock .m-nav {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1.35rem;
  padding: 0.85rem 1.75rem;
  font-size: 0.82rem;
}
.mock .m-nav .brand { font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.01em; }
.mock .m-nav .spacer { margin-left: auto; }
.mock h2.m-h { font-size: clamp(1.6rem, 3.6vw, 2.5rem); letter-spacing: -0.028em; line-height: 1.08; margin: 0; text-wrap: balance; }
.mock p.m-sub { margin: 0; font-size: 0.95rem; max-width: 52ch; }
.mock .m-row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.7rem; align-items: center; }
.mock .m-btn {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.45rem;
  padding: 0.55rem 1rem; border-radius: 7px;
  font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 600;
  text-decoration: none; border: 1px solid transparent;
}

/* terminal strip shared by all mockups */
.term {
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-size: 0.79rem;
  line-height: 1.9;
  padding: 0.85rem 1rem;
  overflow-x: auto;
  white-space: nowrap;
}
.seg {
  display: inline-block;
  padding: 0.1rem 0.72rem 0.1rem 0.6rem;
  margin-right: -0.62rem;
  position: relative;
  clip-path: polygon(0 0, calc(100% - 0.6rem) 0, 100% 50%, calc(100% - 0.6rem) 100%, 0 100%);
}
.seg.first { padding-left: 0.75rem; }
.seg.tail { clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%); padding-right: 0.6rem; }

/* ── Direction A — Calibrated ───────────────────────────────── */
.mock-a {
  --a-bg: #ffffff;
  --a-alt: #f4f6fa;
  --a-ink: #16202e;
  --a-mut: #5b6779;
  --a-rule: #dfe4ec;
  --a-blue: #1f6fd0;
  --a-deep: #10243c;
  background: var(--a-bg);
  color: var(--a-ink);
}
.mock-a .m-nav { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--a-rule); color: var(--a-mut); }
.mock-a .m-nav .brand { color: var(--a-ink); }
.mock-a .m-nav .on { color: var(--a-ink); font-weight: 600; }
.mock-a .m-hero { padding: 2.5rem 0 2.75rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1.1rem; }
.mock-a h2.m-h { color: var(--a-ink); }
.mock-a p.m-sub { color: var(--a-mut); }
.mock-a .m-btn.primary { background: var(--a-blue); color: #fff; }
.mock-a .m-btn.ghost { border-color: var(--a-rule); color: var(--a-ink); }
.mock-a .installbox {
  border: 1px solid var(--a-rule); border-radius: 9px; overflow: hidden; background: var(--a-alt); max-width: 560px;
}
.mock-a .installbox .tabs { display: flex; gap: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--a-rule); font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.72rem; }
.mock-a .installbox .tabs span { padding: 0.45rem 0.85rem; color: var(--a-mut); }
.mock-a .installbox .tabs span.on { color: var(--a-ink); background: var(--a-bg); border-bottom: 2px solid var(--a-blue); font-weight: 600; }
.mock-a .installbox .cmd {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem; padding: 0.7rem 0.9rem;
  font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.79rem; background: var(--a-bg); color: var(--a-ink);
}
.mock-a .installbox .cmd .copy { margin-left: auto; font-size: 0.68rem; color: var(--a-mut); border: 1px solid var(--a-rule); border-radius: 5px; padding: 0.15rem 0.45rem; }
.mock-a .termcard { background: var(--a-deep); border-radius: 9px; margin-top: 0.5rem; }
.mock-a .cards { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 0.85rem; padding-bottom: 2.5rem; }
.mock-a .card { border: 1px solid var(--a-rule); border-radius: 9px; padding: 0.95rem 1rem; background: var(--a-bg); }
.mock-a .card h4 { margin: 0 0 0.3rem; font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--a-ink); }
.mock-a .card p { margin: 0; font-size: 0.79rem; color: var(--a-mut); line-height: 1.5; }
@media (max-width: 700px) { .mock-a .cards { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } }

/* ── Direction B — Terminal Native ──────────────────────────── */
.mock-b {
  --b-bg: #0c0f14;
  --b-panel: #141922;
  --b-wash: #101a26;
  --b-rule: #232c39;
  --b-ink: #e6ecf5;
  --b-mut: #8b98a9;
  --b-blue: #5aa2f5;
  --b-amber: #e6b054;
  --b-green: #5fcf99;
  background: var(--b-bg);
  color: var(--b-ink);
}
.mock-b .m-nav { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--b-rule); color: var(--b-mut); font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.76rem; letter-spacing: 0.02em; }
.mock-b .m-nav .brand { color: var(--b-ink); letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
.mock-b .m-nav .on { color: var(--b-blue); }
.mock-b .m-nav .cta {
  color: var(--b-bg); background: var(--b-blue); font-weight: 700;
  padding: 0.25rem 0.75rem 0.25rem 0.6rem;
  clip-path: polygon(0.5rem 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 0.5rem 100%, 0 50%);
}
.mock-b .m-hero { padding: 2.75rem 0 1.5rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1.05rem; }
.mock-b .eyeb { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.68rem; letter-spacing: 0.18em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--b-amber); }
.mock-b h2.m-h { color: var(--b-ink); }
.mock-b h2.m-h em { font-style: normal; color: var(--b-blue); }
.mock-b p.m-sub { color: var(--b-mut); }
.mock-b .m-btn.primary {
  background: var(--b-blue); color: #08131f; border-radius: 0;
  padding: 0.55rem 1.1rem 0.55rem 0.9rem;
  clip-path: polygon(0.55rem 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 0.55rem 100%, 0 50%);
}
.mock-b .m-btn.ghost { border-color: var(--b-rule); color: var(--b-ink); border-radius: 0; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.78rem; }
.mock-b .termcard { background: #0a0d12; border: 1px solid var(--b-rule); border-radius: 8px; }
.mock-b .termcard .bar { display: flex; gap: 0.35rem; padding: 0.55rem 0.75rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--b-rule); align-items: center; }
.mock-b .termcard .bar i { width: 9px; height: 9px; border-radius: 50%; display: block; }
.mock-b .termcard .bar .lbl { margin-left: auto; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.65rem; color: var(--b-mut); letter-spacing: 0.08em; }
.mock-b .zones { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 0; margin-top: 1.75rem; border-top: 1px solid var(--b-rule); }
.mock-b .zone { padding: 1.1rem 1.15rem 1.35rem; border-right: 1px solid var(--b-rule); }
.mock-b .zone:last-child { border-right: 0; }
.mock-b .zone.z1 { background: #101a26; }
.mock-b .zone.z2 { background: #151424; }
.mock-b .zone.z3 { background: #16211b; }
.mock-b .zone .n { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.66rem; letter-spacing: 0.16em; color: var(--b-mut); }
.mock-b .zone h4 { margin: 0.35rem 0 0.3rem; font-size: 0.92rem; color: var(--b-ink); }
.mock-b .zone p { margin: 0; font-size: 0.78rem; color: var(--b-mut); line-height: 1.5; }
@media (max-width: 700px) { .mock-b .zones { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } .mock-b .zone { border-right: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--b-rule); } }

/* ── Direction C — Studio ───────────────────────────────────── */
.mock-c {
  --c-bg: #0f1016;
  --c-panel: #171922;
  --c-rule: #262a36;
  --c-ink: #eceef5;
  --c-mut: #8c92a4;
  --c-pink: #eb6f92;
  --c-iris: #9b8cf0;
  --c-foam: #74c7c4;
  --c-gold: #f0c674;
  background: var(--c-bg);
  color: var(--c-ink);
}
.mock-c .m-nav { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--c-rule); color: var(--c-mut); font-size: 0.8rem; }
.mock-c .m-nav .brand { color: var(--c-ink); }
.mock-c .m-nav .on { color: var(--c-ink); font-weight: 600; }
.mock-c .m-nav .cta { background: var(--c-iris); color: #10111a; font-weight: 700; padding: 0.28rem 0.8rem; border-radius: 6px; }
.mock-c .studio { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 15.5rem 1fr 13rem; min-height: 300px; }
.mock-c .col { border-right: 1px solid var(--c-rule); padding: 0.9rem 0.95rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.7rem; }
.mock-c .col:last-child { border-right: 0; }
.mock-c .col .lbl { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.63rem; letter-spacing: 0.15em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--c-mut); }
.mock-c .chip {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem;
  font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.72rem;
  padding: 0.32rem 0.5rem; border-radius: 5px;
  border: 1px solid var(--c-rule); background: var(--c-panel); color: var(--c-ink);
}
.mock-c .chip .dot { width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 2px; }
.mock-c .chip .grip { margin-left: auto; color: var(--c-mut); }
.mock-c .stage { background: #0a0b10; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.8rem; align-items: stretch; justify-content: center; padding: 1.25rem 1.1rem; }
.mock-c .stage .pv { background: #12131b; border: 1px solid var(--c-rule); border-radius: 8px; }
.mock-c .stage .pvlbl { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.63rem; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--c-mut); padding: 0 0.1rem; }
.mock-c .swatches { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(6, 1fr); gap: 0.3rem; }
.mock-c .swatches i { aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 4px; display: block; }
.mock-c .out {
  font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.68rem; color: var(--c-mut);
  background: var(--c-panel); border: 1px solid var(--c-rule); border-radius: 6px; padding: 0.5rem 0.6rem;
  white-space: pre-wrap; word-break: break-all; line-height: 1.6;
}
@media (max-width: 820px) { .mock-c .studio { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } .mock-c .col { border-right: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--c-rule); } }

/* ── catalog mockup ─────────────────────────────────────────── */
.mock-cat {
  --k-bg: #0c0f14; --k-panel: #141922; --k-rule: #232c39;
  --k-ink: #e6ecf5; --k-mut: #8b98a9; --k-blue: #5aa2f5; --k-amber: #e6b054;
  background: var(--k-bg); color: var(--k-ink);
}
.mock-cat .cat { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 13.5rem 1fr; min-height: 280px; }
.mock-cat .facets { border-right: 1px solid var(--k-rule); padding: 1rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem; }
.mock-cat .facets .grp { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.35rem; }
.mock-cat .facets .lbl { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.62rem; letter-spacing: 0.15em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--k-mut); }
.mock-cat .facets label { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.45rem; font-size: 0.78rem; color: var(--k-mut); }
.mock-cat .facets label .box { width: 12px; height: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--k-rule); border-radius: 3px; display: block; }
.mock-cat .facets label.on { color: var(--k-ink); }
.mock-cat .facets label.on .box { background: var(--k-blue); border-color: var(--k-blue); }
.mock-cat .facets label .ct { margin-left: auto; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.68rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
.mock-cat .results { padding: 1rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.8rem; }
.mock-cat .searchbar { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; border: 1px solid var(--k-rule); border-radius: 7px; padding: 0.45rem 0.7rem; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.78rem; color: var(--k-mut); background: var(--k-panel); }
.mock-cat .searchbar .kbd { margin-left: auto; font-size: 0.65rem; border: 1px solid var(--k-rule); border-radius: 4px; padding: 0.05rem 0.3rem; }
.mock-cat .grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(180px, 1fr)); gap: 0.7rem; }
.mock-cat .item { border: 1px solid var(--k-rule); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--k-panel); padding: 0.7rem 0.8rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.4rem; }
.mock-cat .item .nm { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.82rem; color: var(--k-ink); }
.mock-cat .item .ds { font-size: 0.73rem; color: var(--k-mut); line-height: 1.45; }
.mock-cat .item .tags { display: flex; gap: 0.3rem; flex-wrap: wrap; }
.mock-cat .item .tag { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.6rem; letter-spacing: 0.06em; padding: 0.08rem 0.35rem; border-radius: 3px; border: 1px solid var(--k-rule); color: var(--k-mut); }
.mock-cat .item .tag.hot { color: var(--k-amber); border-color: currentColor; }
@media (max-width: 700px) { .mock-cat .cat { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } .mock-cat .facets { border-right: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--k-rule); } }

/* ── phase list ─────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.phases { display: grid; gap: 1px; background: var(--rule); border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 8px; overflow: hidden; }
.phase { background: var(--panel); padding: 1.05rem 1.2rem; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 5.5rem 1fr; gap: 0 1.25rem; }
.phase .no { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 0.72rem; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--accent); padding-top: 0.15rem; }
.phase h4 { font-size: 0.95rem; margin: 0 0 0.3rem; }

<header class="masthead">
  <div class="wrap stack gap-6">
    <div class="stack gap-4">
      <p class="eyebrow">Design & information architecture proposal</p>
      <h1>ohmyposh.dev renders everything except the prompt.</h1>
      <p class="lede">
        The site sells a tool whose entire value is what appears on screen, then shows almost none of it.
        Three redesign directions follow, from a token-level refit to a full studio rebuild — each paired
        with a navigation architecture that shortens the path from landing to running.
      </p>
    </div>
    <div class="meta-row">
      <span><b>Stack</b> Docusaurus 3.10 · Algolia · Azure SWA</span>
      <span><b>Surface</b> 153 docs · 117 segments · 124 themes</span>
      <span><b>Benchmarked</b> 12 tool sites</span>
    </div>
  </div>
</header>

<section class="band">
  <div class="wrap stack gap-8">
    <div class="stack gap-3">
      <p class="eyebrow">01 — Where we are</p>
      <h2 style="font-size:1.65rem;">The homepage is still the 2020 Docusaurus scaffold</h2>
      <p class="lede">
        Two buttons, three emoji paragraphs, one static PNG — about 130 lines total. Everything that would
        make a visitor install has to be found somewhere else.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="stat-grid">
      <div class="stat"><span class="n">130</span><span class="l">lines in the entire homepage</span></div>
      <div class="stat"><span class="n">11</span><span class="l">top-level sidebar entries, all emoji-prefixed</span></div>
      <div class="stat"><span class="n warn">28,093<span style="font-size:0.6em">px</span></span><span class="l">height of the themes page — 124 PNGs, 8 MB, no filter</span></div>
      <div class="stat"><span class="n warn">0</span><span class="l">segment reference pages showing what the segment looks like</span></div>
      <div class="stat"><span class="n">117</span><span class="l">segments, reachable only by guessing a category</span></div>
      <div class="stat"><span class="n warn">3</span><span class="l">clicks minimum from homepage to an install command</span></div>
    </div>

    <div class="stack gap-4">
      <h3 style="font-size:1.05rem;">Concrete defects found in the codebase</h3>
      <div class="findings">
        <div class="finding">
          <span class="sev block">Blocking</span>
          <p><b>“Get Started →” lands on a theory page.</b> <code>configuration/introduction.mdx</code> carries <code>slug: /</code>, so the primary homepage CTA opens an essay about blocks and segments — not an install command. The sidebar’s actual first item is Getting Started › Installation › Windows, which the CTA never reaches.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="finding">
          <span class="sev block">Blocking</span>
          <p><b>No index pages exist.</b> Getting Started, Segments, and all eight segment sub-groups are bare categories — clicking them only expands a tree. <code>static/llms.txt</code> already links <code>/docs/segments/overview</code> and <code>/docs/configuration/overview</code>; neither page exists, and <code>onBrokenLinks: 'ignore'</code> hides it.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="finding">
          <span class="sev block">Blocking</span>
          <p><b>Segment discovery depends on guessing a bucket.</b> <code>kubectl</code>, <code>helm</code> and <code>argocd</code> live under CLI, not Cloud. <code>docker</code> is CLI. <code>winget</code> is System. Every group is <code>collapsed: true</code> by default, so the default view of 117 segments shows nothing.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="finding">
          <span class="sev friction">Friction</span>
          <p><b>The theme gallery is one 124-image scroll.</b> No search, no tags, no filter, no per-theme URL, no way to apply one. The Nerd-Font requirement is a sentence of prose, not a facet. It is also one of only two homepage CTAs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="finding">
          <span class="sev friction">Friction</span>
          <p><b>The FAQ absorbs everything with no home.</b> 24 headings covering PowerShell, fonts, Windows Terminal, JetBrains, Conda, venv, Zsh, Fish, Xonsh, Vim and posh-git. There is no troubleshooting section, no per-shell page and no per-terminal page.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="finding">
          <span class="sev friction">Friction</span>
          <p><b>Orphan and near-orphan docs.</b> <code>docs/auth.mdx</code> is in no sidebar — only reachable via an OAuth redirect. <code>Advanced</code> is a category with exactly one child. <code>dsc</code>, <code>themes</code>, <code>share</code>, <code>faq</code>, <code>migrating</code> and <code>contributors</code> float loose at root.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="finding">
          <span class="sev friction">Friction</span>
          <p><b>Navbar priorities are inverted.</b> Sponsor and Swag sit in primary left nav beside Docs and Blog, above a non-closeable sponsor bar. The blog has averaged under one post a year since 2022. Themes and Segments — the two things people actually come for — are not in the nav at all.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="finding">
          <span class="sev polish">Polish</span>
          <p><b>The CSS has hash-coupled selectors.</b> <code>a.getStarted_Sjon</code> and <code>.themedImage_ToTc</code> target generated CSS-module hashes and break silently on upgrade. <code>--ifm-color-primary-lightest</code> is <code>rgb(8,9,10)</code> — near-black. <code>--ifm-font-family-monospace</code> is set to <code>"Inter"</code>. Fira Code is fetched from Google Fonts and never referenced.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

      <h3 style="font-size:1.05rem;">The four idioms</h3>
      <div class="findings">
        <div class="finding"><span class="sev polish">Idiom 1</span><p><b>The hero is the install command.</b> Bun, Atuin, Astro and Tauri all put a copyable command above the fold, with an OS or package-manager toggle and the current version in the button. Nobody makes you click through.</p></div>
        <div class="finding"><span class="sev polish">Idiom 2</span><p><b>Product surfaces are rendered in the DOM, never screenshotted.</b> Crisp at any DPI, selectable, theme-reactive, diffable in git, indexable. PNG galleries now read as dated — which is exactly what our themes page is.</p></div>
        <div class="finding"><span class="sev polish">Idiom 3</span><p><b>Dark-first, but zoned.</b> One flat black is out. Warp tints section washes purple/blue/green/amber over a near-black ground; Atuin runs <code>#0f1722</code> with a green and warm-cream pair. Calibrated neutral ramps plus one saturated accent — no gradient mesh, no glass, no grain.</p></div>
        <div class="finding"><span class="sev polish">Idiom 4</span><p><b>Typography carries the brand.</b> Zed self-hosts four families; Ghostty picked Pretendard; Atuin pairs DM Sans with Space Mono. The sites that read as templates are the ones on stock Inter over a stock generator theme — Starship and Oh My Posh, both.</p></div>
      </div>
      <div class="callout">
        <b>Free win, one line:</b> Starship prepends <code>"Nerd Font"</code> to its monospace stack, so Nerd Font glyphs render correctly in code blocks for anyone who has the font installed. Every powerline character in our docs currently falls back to tofu for visitors without it.

        <thead>
          <tr><th></th><th>A · Calibrated</th><th>B · Terminal Native</th><th>C · Studio</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Effort</td><td>Days</td><td>Weeks</td><td>A quarter, incremental</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Platform</td><td>Docusaurus, unchanged</td><td>Docusaurus + custom React pages</td><td>Docusaurus for prose, app for the rest</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Pairs with</td><td>IA-1</td><td>IA-2</td><td>IA-3</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Kills the PNG gallery</td><td class="verdict down">no</td><td class="verdict up">yes — DOM renders</td><td class="verdict up">yes — editable renders</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Segment previews</td><td class="verdict down">no</td><td class="verdict up">static live render</td><td class="verdict up">interactive</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Visually distinct from Starship</td><td>somewhat</td><td class="verdict up">decisively</td><td class="verdict up">no comparison</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Maintenance load</td><td>lower than today</td><td>renderer to maintain</td><td>a real app to maintain</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Risk</td><td>none</td><td>renderer fidelity vs the Go engine</td><td>scope, and a second implementation to keep honest</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>

    <div class="callout">
      <b>Recommendation: B with IA-2, built so that C stays reachable.</b> The prompt renderer is the load-bearing
      piece in both — build it once, behind a stable interface that takes a config object and mock context and returns

    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ══════════════════════════════ PHASING ══════════════════════════════ -->
<section class="band">
  <div class="wrap stack gap-8">
    <div class="stack gap-3">
      <p class="eyebrow">06 — Sequence</p>
      <h2 style="font-size:1.65rem;">Order of work</h2>

    </div>

    <div class="phases">
      <div class="phase">
        <span class="no">Phase 0</span>
        <div>
          <h4>Stop the bleeding</h4>
          <p>Pure bug fixes, no design decisions required.</p>
          <ul>
            <li>Move <code>slug: /</code> off <code>configuration/introduction</code>; add a docs hub page.</li>
            <li>Add <code>/docs/segments</code> and <code>/docs/configuration</code> indexes — <code>llms.txt</code> already links them.</li>
            <li>Flip <code>onBrokenLinks</code> to <code>throw</code> and fix what falls out.</li>
            <li>Delete the hash-coupled CSS selectors; fix <code>--ifm-font-family-monospace</code>; drop the unused Fira Code request; correct <code>--ifm-color-primary-lightest</code>.</li>
            <li>Prepend <code>"Nerd Font"</code> to the monospace stack.</li>
            <li>Put <code>auth.mdx</code> in the sidebar; collapse the one-child Advanced category.</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="phase">
        <span class="no">Phase 1</span>
        <div>
          <h4>Homepage and nav</h4>
          <p>Direction B applied to the two highest-traffic surfaces.</p>
          <ul>
            <li>Rebuild the hero: install box with OS toggle, version in the button, DOM-rendered prompt.</li>
            <li>Promote Themes and Segments into primary nav; move Sponsor, Swag and Blog into Community.</li>
            <li>Retire the non-closeable announcement bar in favour of a footer sponsor block.</li>
            <li>Token pass: neutral ramp, type scale, chevron geometry, zoned dark sections.</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="phase">
        <span class="no">Phase 2</span>
        <div>
          <h4>The renderer</h4>
          <p>The load-bearing investment. One function: config + mock context → DOM.</p>
          <ul>
            <li>Reuse <code>segment_data.json</code> as the fixture context; it already covers every segment.</li>
            <li>Verify fidelity against the Go engine in CI — render every bundled theme both ways and diff the ANSI.</li>
            <li>Ship it first as a build-time renderer, so there is no client-side cost yet.</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="phase">
        <span class="no">Phase 3</span>
        <div>
          <h4>Catalogs</h4>
          <p>Point the renderer at the two large surfaces.</p>
          <ul>
            <li><code>/themes</code>: faceted gallery, per-theme URLs, live renders, one-click apply command. Deletes 8 MB of PNGs.</li>
            <li><code>/segments</code>: faceted catalog with badge column, each card previewing its own output.</li>
            <li>Embed the same preview at the top of every segment reference page.</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="phase">
        <span class="no">Phase 4</span>
        <div>
          <h4>Docs restructure</h4>
          <p>IA-2 in full, once the two catalogs have left <code>/docs</code>.</p>
          <ul>
            <li>Split the FAQ into Troubleshooting by shell, terminal and editor.</li>
            <li>Separate hand-written Configure prose from a generated Reference tier — the Bun split.</li>
            <li>Drop emoji from sidebar labels; order segments by usage, not alphabet.</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="phase">
        <span class="no">Phase 5</span>
        <div>
          <h4>Studio, if the renderer holds up</h4>
          <p>Only worth starting once phases 2–3 have proven fidelity in production.</p>
          <ul>
            <li>Editor around the existing renderer; config encoded in the URL.</li>
            <li>“Open in Studio” from every theme and every segment page.</li>
            <li>Short-link service so <code>--config</code> can point at a shared prompt.</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ══════════════════════════════ OPEN ══════════════════════════════ -->
<section class="band">
  <div class="wrap stack gap-6">
    <div class="stack gap-3">
      <p class="eyebrow">07 — Open questions</p>
      <h2 style="font-size:1.65rem;">Decisions that change the plan</h2>
    </div>
    <div class="findings">
      <div class="finding"><span class="sev polish">Q1</span><p><b>Stay on Docusaurus?</b> Astro + Starlight is what Biome and Tauri run, and it makes custom app-like pages far cheaper than Docusaurus swizzling. Migrating 153 docs is real work but mostly mechanical. Direction B is doable either way; direction C is materially easier on Astro.</p></div>
      <div class="finding"><span class="sev polish">Q2</span><p><b>Second renderer, or compile the real one?</b> A JS renderer risks drifting from the Go engine. The alternative is compiling the engine to WASM and rendering the truth — heavier, but there is then only one implementation to trust.</p></div>
      <div class="finding"><span class="sev polish">Q3</span><p><b>Nerd Font glyphs on the web.</b> Live previews need a subset Nerd Font served from the site, or the powerline separators will render as tofu for most visitors. Licensing and weight both need a look.</p></div>
      <div class="finding"><span class="sev polish">Q4</span><p><b>Does the blog stay?</b> Six posts since 2022. Either fold it into a Community section alongside release notes, or retire it and let the changelog carry that job.</p></div>
      <div class="finding"><span class="sev polish">Q5</span><p><b>Where does sponsorship live?</b> The permanent announcement bar and the two primary-nav slots are the most valuable real estate on the site and currently earn less than a well-placed footer block would.</p></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<footer class="end">
  <div class="wrap">Analysis phase only — no code changed. Mockups are DOM, not images; view source to lift the chevron geometry.</div>
</footer>

</div>

content.text:
Proposal live: **https://claude.ai/code/artifact/7e76d82e-c9b9-4c14-888b-d0e1f540d320**

Mockups are DOM — powerline chevrons cut with `clip-path`, no images. That itself is the argument.

## Core finding

Site sells a thing whose whole value is pixels on screen. Shows almost none of them. Starship has same disease (logo-only hero). Atuin, Zed, Bun all render product surfaces in DOM now — screenshots read as dated.

**Hard defects, not opinions:**
- `configuration/introduction.mdx` has `slug: /` — "Get Started →" lands on block/segment theory, not an install command. 3 clicks to a command.
- Zero index pages. `static/llms.txt` already links `/docs/segments/overview` + `/docs/configuration/overview`; neither exists. `onBrokenLinks: 'ignore'` hides it.
- Themes page: 28,093px, 124 PNGs, 8MB, no filter/tags/per-theme URL/apply.
- 117 segments, all groups `collapsed: true`, discovery = guess the bucket (`kubectl`/`helm`/`argocd` are CLI, not Cloud).
- `custom.css` targets generated hashes (`a.getStarted_Sjon`, `.themedImage_ToTc`). `--ifm-font-family-monospace: "Inter"`. `--ifm-color-primary-lightest: rgb(8,9,10)`. Fira Code fetched, never used.
- `auth.mdx` orphaned — no sidebar entry, reachable only via OAuth redirect.

## Three directions

| | A · Calibrated | B · Terminal Native | C · Studio |
|---|---|---|---|
| Effort | days | weeks | a quarter |
| IA | IA-1 Tidy | IA-2 Four doors | IA-3 Studio-first |
| Kills PNG gallery | no | yes | yes, editable |

**Recommend B + IA-2, built so C stays reachable.** Load-bearing piece in both is one prompt renderer: `config + mock context → DOM`. `segment_data.json` is already a complete fixture. `export_themes.mjs` already knows author + bg per theme. Build renderer once behind a stable interface; B uses it at build time, C later drives it from an editor.

IA-2 moves Themes and Segments *out* of `/docs` into faceted first-class sections, splits Configure prose from a generated Reference tier (Bun's move), and gives Sponsor/Swag/Blog an honest home in Community instead of primary nav.

## Open decisions that change the plan

1. Stay on Docusaurus, or move to Astro + Starlight (Biome, Tauri)? C is materially cheaper on Astro.
2. JS renderer (drift risk vs Go engine) or compile engine to WASM (one truth, heavier)?
3. Nerd Font subset served from site — otherwise live previews are tofu. Licensing + weight.
4. Blog: 6 posts since 2022. Fold into Community with release notes, or retire.

Phase 0 in the artifact is all bug fixes, no design calls — shippable immediately, independent of which direction you pick. Say the word and I'll plan it.

content.thinking:
I'm seeing the full pipeline now: theme JSON files get exported to images through oh-my-posh's config export command, which generates an ANSI string that's then rasterized to PNG using a fork of termshot that leverages graphics libraries for parsing and rendering.

The core logic for segment evaluation, template rendering, and color resolution all lives in Go modules like the prompt engine and config handlers. For the studio, the key insight is that the existing `applyDataFile` mechanism already makes the engine hermetic — by populating segment and environment data from fixtures instead of live system calls, I can compile the Go engine to WebAssembly and run it entirely in the browser without needing to stub out filesystem or execution dependencies.

Alternatively, I could add a server-side render endpoint that shells the real binary with `--data` and returns structured output, trading network latency for zero drift. Or I could reimplement just the presentation layer in TypeScript while keeping evaluation in Go. The cleanest approach is to have the engine emit structured output — a list of styled text runs with foreground, background, and style information — rather than raw ANSI, so the JavaScript side only needs to map that to DOM spans. Let me check if the terminal package already has an HTML or structured export option.

Now I'm structuring the answer: starting with where the pipeline logic currently lives, explaining why the web can't reuse it since it's all Go, pointing out that `--data` already makes the engine hermetic, laying out three options with a recommendation, and identifying what's missing—a structured export format instead of ANSI output.

content.text:
Today it comes from the Go binary. Nothing on the web renders anything.

## Current pipeline

[export_themes.mjs](website/export_themes.mjs) is a shell-out loop:

```
themes/*.omp.json
  → oh-my-posh config export image --config X --data segment_data.json
      --background-color Y --author Z
  → prompt.Engine.Primary()          ANSI string
  → cli/image/image.go               rasterize (fork of homeport/termshot,
                                      fogleman/gg + opentype)
  → website/static/img/themes/X.png
  → append markdown into docs/themes.md
```

Everything that decides what a prompt looks like is Go: [prompt/engine.go](src/prompt/engine.go) (864 lines), [config/segment.go](src/config/segment.go), `segments/*`, `template/`, `color/`, `terminal/writer.go`. `image.go` is 920 lines of rasterizer that exists only because there was no other way to get pixels into markdown.

No WASM build, no JS renderer, no render endpoint. Website has zero of it.

## The wedge already exists

[cli/data.go](src/cli/data.go) — `applyDataFile` sets `flags.SegmentData` + `flags.EnvData`, and segments replay from that instead of shelling out to `git`, `kubectl`, `az`. `segment_data.json` covers every segment.

That makes the engine **hermetic**: no exec, no filesystem walk, no HTTP. That's precisely the property a browser build needs. `--data` was built for screenshots, but it's the studio's foundation.

## Three ways to get it on the web

**1. WASM — single source of truth.** `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm` build of the engine. With `SegmentData` populated the hot path already avoids exec/fs; cache and HTTP need stubs. Ship the config from the editor, get output back. No drift, ever.

**2. Render endpoint — cheapest.** `website/api` is already Azure Functions ([api/mcp](website/api/mcp), [api/auth](website/api/auth)). Add `/api/render`: POST config + data, shell the real binary, return output. Zero drift, zero WASM work, one round-trip per edit (debounce ~120ms). Also replaces the PNG build step for the gallery.

**3. TypeScript reimplementation — don't.** Template engine, 117 segments, color resolution, palettes, gradients, powerline joining. Guaranteed drift, and the drift is invisible until a user reports a wrong prompt.

## Missing piece either way

Both 1 and 2 return **ANSI**, so the browser needs an ANSI parser — same problem `image.go` already solved badly once.

Better: add a structured emitter alongside the image one. `terminal/writer.go` already tracks foreground, background, and style per run — it just flattens them to escape codes. Emit them instead:

```
config export render --format json --data segment_data.json
→ [{ "text": "alice", "fg": "#191724", "bg": "#eb6f92", "bold": true }, …]
```

Then JS maps runs to spans. No parser, no fidelity guesswork, and it's testable in Go against the same golden files the ANSI writer uses.

**Recommendation:** endpoint + structured export first (small, no drift, unblocks Phase 2–3 of the artifact). WASM later only if the studio needs sub-100ms interactive feedback. That ordering also lets you delete `cli/image/image.go` — 920 lines of rasterizer whose only consumer is the gallery you're replacing.
